page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V2 processor model running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 128 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory performance and efficient data processing capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3269.65 and demonstrated high throughput in PassMark database operations at 49533.61. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, reaching 3959.51 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 343.0 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In compute-focused tests, the server recorded a PassMark CPU score of 29085.47 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 58166.14. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also performed strongly, with gzip compression reaching 32.36 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scaling to 391.36 GB/sec in multi-threaded scenarios.

With its dedicated ARM cores and high memory bandwidth, the c4a-standard-32 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that benefit from high resource density and predictable execution without hyperthreading overhead. It is highly suited for database operations, as evidenced by its top-tier database benchmark results and strong Redis performance of 68.8 million SET operations per second. Additionally, the instance is well-suited for static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 76.05 GB/sec, and moderate language model inference tasks, processing 7B model text generation at 31.42 tokens per second.
